name: Windows Forensic Artifacts — NTFS, Execution, Persistence & Zone.Identifier
description: Key Windows forensic artifact locations and analysis. NTFS: $MFT (file metadata), $J USN Journal (file ops), LNK files, ADS/Zone.Identifier (MotW), VSC. Execution artifacts: Prefetch (C:\Windows\Prefetch), ShimCache (HKLM\SYSTEM\...\AppCompatCache), Amcache (C:\Windows\AppCompat\Programs\Amcache.hve), BAM (HKLM\SYSTEM\...\bam\State\UserSettings\{SID}), UserAssist, RunMRU. Persistence: Registry Run keys (HKCU/HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run), Scheduled Tasks (C:\Windows\System32\Tasks), Services (HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services), Startup folder. SRUM: C:\Windows\System32\sru\SRUDB.dat (network usage). Zone.Identifier ZoneId=3 = Internet Zone — present on all downloaded files.
source: CDSA Module 13: Introduction to Digital Forensics
notes:
=== DIGITAL FORENSICS PROCESS ===
1. Identification  → What evidence exists and where
2. Collection      → Acquire evidence (forensically sound, write-blocked)
3. Examination     → Extract relevant data
4. Analysis        → Interpret findings
5. Presentation    → Report conclusions

=== NTFS ARTIFACT LOCATIONS ===
$MFT           → Every file/dir record, full metadata, timestamps (MAC(b))
$J (USN Jrnl)  → <KAPE_out>\<Drive>\$Extend\$J — file create/rename/delete/overwrite
$LogFile       → NTFS transaction log
LNK Files      → C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Recent\
Jump Lists     → C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Recent\AutomaticDestinations\
Shellbags      → HKCU\Software\Classes\Local Settings\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Shell
Thumb Cache    → C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Windows\Explorer\thumbcache_*.db
Recycle Bin    → C:\$Recycle.Bin\{SID}\$R* (content) + $I* (metadata: orig path, deletion time)
VSC            → Volume Shadow Copies — \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopyN\
SRUM           → C:\Windows\System32\sru\SRUDB.dat (SQLite — network bytes, process, user)

=== MAC(b) TIMESTAMPS ===
M = Last Modified (content change)
A = Last Accessed
C = $MFT record Changed (attribute/metadata change)
b = Birth (file creation time)

Timestomping (T1070.006):
  $STANDARD_INFORMATION: modifiable by user-space tools (e.g., Meterpreter timestomp)
  $FILE_NAME: only updated by Windows kernel — reveals real creation/modification time
  Detection: SI modified ≠ FN modified → timestomping
  Tool: MFTECmd deep entry dump shows both SI and FN timestamps

  Detect with MFTECmd:
    MFTECmd.exe -f $MFT --de <MFT_entry_hex>     → dump both $SI and $FN timestamps
  Detect with Autopsy: File Metadata tab → compare $FILE_NAME MFT Modified vs $STANDARD_INFORMATION File Modified

=== EXECUTION ARTIFACTS ===

--- Prefetch ---
Location: C:\Windows\Prefetch\
Naming:   EXENAME-HASH.pf
Contents: run count, last run time, first run time, dirs/files referenced
Suspicious: executables from %TEMP%, Downloads, Tasks
Parse: PECmd.exe (Eric Zimmerman)

--- ShimCache (AppCompatCache) ---
Registry: HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Control\Session Manager\AppCompatCache
Contents: full file paths + timestamps + execution flag (Windows 7 = yes/no; Win10+ = no exec flag)
View in Registry Explorer → bookmark "AppCompatCache"
Parse: AppCompatCacheParser.exe -f SYSTEM --csv <dir>

--- Amcache ---
Location: C:\Windows\AppCompat\Programs\Amcache.hve
Contents: execution path, first executed time, deleted time, first install, file SHA1 hash
Parse: AmcacheParser.exe -f Amcache.hve --csv <dir>
→ Load output in Timeline Explorer

--- BAM (Background Activity Moderator) ---
Kernel driver; records last execution time per program per user
Registry: HKLM\SYSTEM\ControlSet001\Services\bam\State\UserSettings\{USER-SID}
View in Registry Explorer → bookmark "bam"
Parse with RegRipper: rip.exe -r SYSTEM -p bam

--- UserAssist ---
Registry: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\UserAssist
Contents: GUI app launch counts + timestamps (ROT13 encoded)

--- RunMRU ---
Registry: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU
Contents: commands typed in Win+R Run dialog

=== ZONE.IDENTIFIER / MARK OF THE WEB (MotW) ===
All internet-downloaded files receive a Zone.Identifier ADS:
  Zone IDs: 0=Local, 1=Intranet, 2=Trusted, 3=Internet, 4=Restricted
  ZoneId=3 = downloaded from internet

ADS also contains:
  ZoneTransfer block:
    ReferrerUrl = page that linked to the download
    HostUrl     = direct download URL (source URL of file)

View ADS streams:
  PowerShell list:   Get-Item * -Stream Zone.Identifier -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
  PowerShell read:   Get-Content <file> -Stream Zone.Identifier
  CLI:               more < file.exe:Zone.Identifier

Impact: Word/Office opens internet-origin files in Protected View
View in Autopsy: Downloads folder → .Zone.Identifier ADS attribute
View in Prefetch (PECmd): "files loaded" section includes :Zone.Identifier entries

=== USN JOURNAL ($J) ===
Tracks: FileCreate, FileDelete, Rename, DataOverwrite, DataExtend, StreamChange
Location: <KAPE_output>\<Drive>\$Extend\$J

Parse with MFTECmd:
  MFTECmd.exe -f $J --csv <output_dir> --csvf MFT-J.csv

Filter with PowerShell (time range + file extensions):
  $time1 = [DateTime]::ParseExact("2023-08-10 09:00:00.000000", "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.ffffff", $null)
  $time2 = [DateTime]::ParseExact("2023-08-10 10:00:00.000000", "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.ffffff", $null)
  Import-Csv usn_output.csv | Where-Object { $_.'FileName' -match '\.exe$|\.ps1$|\.bat$|\.iso$|\.lnk$' } |
    Where-Object { $_.timestamp -as [DateTime] -ge $time1 -and $_.timestamp -as [DateTime] -lt $time2 }

Also parse with usn.py:
  python usn.py -f $UsnJrnl:$J -o usn_output.csv -c

Key pattern: .crdownload extension = Chrome partial/in-progress download
Key pattern: STREAM_CHANGE + NAMED_DATA_EXTEND on .iso = Zone.Identifier ADS written = internet download

=== PERSISTENCE LOCATIONS ===
Registry Run Keys (autostart at logon):
  HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
  HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce
  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run        ← system-wide
  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce
  HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Winlogon  (Userinit, Shell values)
  HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Shell Folders

Scheduled Tasks:
  C:\Windows\System32\Tasks\
  View with Autoruns tool → Scheduled Tasks tab
  Parse: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks

Services:
  HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\

Startup Folder:
  C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\
  C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup\

Autoruns tool (.arn files):
  Logon tab → Run keys
  Scheduled Tasks tab
  Services tab
  SHA256 hash for each entry → submit to VirusTotal
  Get-FileHash -Algorithm SHA256 <path>   → hash executable for VT lookup

=== SRUM (System Resource Usage Monitor) ===
Location: C:\Windows\System32\sru\SRUDB.dat (SQLite)
Contents: per-process network bytes sent/received, per-app usage
View via Autopsy → Data Artifacts → Run Programs → SRUDB.dat
Useful for: quantifying data exfiltration (e.g., 430526981 bytes = ~430MB transferred)
